requirement: The `habeas-requirements` skill MUST direct agents, once every group is decided, to commit the agreed requirements of all groups in one commit before any implementation, leaving out uncommitted edits the user said do not belong to the task.
rationale:
**Verdict:** the test adequately checks the requirement. I read the skill text in `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md#section[Habeas%20requirements]/section[Workflow]` and the test helpers.

The requirement says the skill must direct agents to do four things:
- commit once every group is decided;
- commit all groups in one commit;
- commit before any implementation;
- leave out uncommitted edits the user said do not belong to the task.

`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[the_requirements_skill_commits_every_group_together_before_code]` covers each of these:
- **Single commit, before code.** `step_of` finds the workflow step that contains "then commit it, all groups together, before any code". The assertions use that step's number, so the test fails if the phrase is removed or reworded. The phrase covers both "all groups together" and "before any code".
- **Excluding unrelated edits.** `step(SKILL, commit).contains("leave out unrelated edits found in step 1")` checks that the commit step carries the exclusion. Step 1 of the skill tells the agent to ask the user whether uncommitted edits belong to the task, so "unrelated edits found in step 1" is the skill's wording for edits the user said do not belong.
- **Once every group is decided.** `commit > step_of(SKILL, "**Gate:**")` checks that the commit step comes after the step holding the gate. The gate text says there is no commit until the user has agreed to, rejected, or deferred every group.

The test is a text-structure check, so a few points about its scope:
- Ordering against the "Implement and test" step is asserted in `fn[the_requirements_skill_commits_agreed_requirements_before_code]`. That test cites the parent requirement. It is not needed here, because the "before any code" phrase assertion already covers this obligation.
- A different test could miss the exact wording, but this one's assertions would break on removal of any of the four directives, so I found no plausible violating change it would accept.
